newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Holiday slows year-end trade at Kuwait bourse.
newsitem.headline: Holiday slows year-end trade at Kuwait bourse.

text.p: In thinner, holiday-affected trade, the share index on the Kuwait Stock Exchange edged fractionally lower in the last trading week of 1996, dealers said on Thursday.
"Many dealers are on holiday and others want to see how company results are going to be," said a private dealer. "Some shares rose on talk about good profit."
Listed firms are expected to report their annual results in the next few weeks.
"The market is fine. We expect active trade in 1997," said a portfolio manager.
The index fell 2.8 points to 1,905.6 points. Losers led gainers 22-15, while 13 stocks were unchanged, figures released by the exchange on Thursday showed.

A January bad debt repayment deadline for private investors had a "little impact" on trade, said a dealer. Private debtors involved in a programme to settle $20 billion in bad debt owed to the state have to pay a portion of their debt by January 7.
Trade traditionally eases ahead of debt payments.
Total value traded fell to a daily average 19.7 million dinars ($66 million) in the four-day week, shortened by the New Year holiday, compared to a daily average 25.7 million dinars the week before.
Volume fell to an average 52.1 million shares a day from 90.2 million shares the previous week.
Banks were the most active sector in terms of value traded with 25.9 million dinars, followed by investment firms with 16.9 million and services firms with 14.1 million.
National Bank, Commercial Bank, Gulf Bank, Coast Development, Securities Group, United Realty, National Industries and Mobile Telecommunications were among the most active shares.
Only nationals of Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Kuwait -- can trade on the exchange. Foreign residents can invest through mutual funds.
Kuwait is considering opening trade for foreign investors.
